judged_text: Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback predicate is tautologically dead: in the `else` branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match, making `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` always `undefined` and causing googleapis 'Missing required parameters: calendarId' errors — breaking reschedule/cancel of any booking whose stored reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (legacy and new fallback-created references), leaving stale/orphaned events and double-booked calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value (typically `undefined`/`null`), so it will almost never match and `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent` (which falls back to `"primary"`), `updateEvent` does not show a fallback, so it will pass an undefined `calendarId` to `calendar.events.update`, which is consistent with googleapis "Missing required parameters: calendarId". The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent`/`calendarId` computation as well.
